title: GSA-derived automated native SDK testing
integration_generation: Classic MCSDK with KSSIDP. Adapt to the supplied artifact; not standalone IDPSDK, SuperApp or Flutter test qualification.

qualification.note: GSA source patterns reviewed; this test recipe and runner templates have not been executed against customer apps. Earlier activation/login acceptance does not qualify these suites.

prerequisites: Required: run sdk_native_preflight against the selected environment before building or activation. Native KSSIDP uses BDDKEnrollment/BDDKLogin, useTokenBasedLogin=true, astServerBackend=maverick and login header X-KOBIL-ASTUSERID. The WebView alternative is KSTrustedWebView with explicit deployment clients. Missing clients or incompatible bindings block progress; never create substitute flows.
Select native platform, exact SDK artifact, app build, dedicated test app ID, device and explicit customer-configured backend/client flow. Never recommend SuperApp Login V2 for native Android/iOS.
Register app/version with an existing registration user and package valid SDK config JWT and certificate assets before attempting activation.
Provision unique test users and one-time activation codes through MCP IDP/AST tools. Keep backend administrative credentials in the configured credential provider, outside app/test binaries.
Identify destructive reset behavior before running: use a dedicated app/container and fixtures owned by this run. Preserve existing app users and device settings.
sequence: Separate model/unit checks (no real backend), SDK event integration checks on supported devices, and UI/backend end-to-end checks. Report each layer independently.

Prepare a run manifest with artifact checksum/version, app revision, platform/OS, selected test cases, non-secret fixture identifiers and cleanup ownership. Discover actual runner tasks/schemes in the target app.

Create fixtures before the UI action and verify backend calls succeeded. Register listeners before dispatch; use bounded event/predicate waits and fail on timeout. Never substitute fixed sleeps or an unbounded latch for completion.

For fresh activation assert Start success, activation-required and no users; submit fixture inputs through a private test channel; assert SDK activation result and the intended user/device association.

Preserve the activated app data within the same test, terminate/relaunch the process, assert login-required with the same stored user and successful returning login. A successful activation dialog alone is insufficient.
For TMS assert transaction identity, payload, UI action, SDK terminal result and backend terminal status. A request being accepted or a dialog appearing does not establish completion.

Add wrong/expired activation-code and wrong-PIN tests only for dedicated fixtures with known lockout/reset policy; assert failure and absence of an unintended state transition. Keep skipped/disabled cases visible.

Extend the selected feature matrix with property set/get round trips, change-PIN old/new credential behavior, reactivation, add/delete users and queued/background/multiple TMS delivery. Use exact result/status assertions, expected counts and correlated transaction IDs; do not infer that a skipped plan entry ran.

On every failure retain Warning, RuntimeError and FatalError errorType, errorDescription and unsigned errorCode with timestamps and last SDK state; attach runner results and SDK log archive before reset. Do not log secrets.

In finally/teardown unregister listeners, close helpers and remove only run-owned fixtures; record cleanup failures separately so they do not hide the original failure. Restore any changed device settings.
expected_result: A per-case report distinguishes passed, failed, skipped and not_run, with bounded waits, SDK/backend state assertions and cleanup evidence. Test names and source presence are not evidence of execution.
failure_handling: Android positiveflowtest activationLoginTransactionTest asserts activation UI success and submits/confirms a transaction; it does not explicitly verify cold returning login or backend terminal TMS status. Add those assertions.

Android integratedUnitTest contains an ignored test with unbounded CountDownLatch.await. The inspected adapter dispatches TriggerBannerEvent but only logs TransactionEndEvent; do not copy it as a complete transaction observer.
Some multiflow negative cases are commented out. Count them as missing coverage, not passing tests.
Android Orchestrator clearPackageData and explicit clearAppData erase activation state. Keep activation plus cold login in one test, or use an explicitly controlled persistent fixture.
GSA helper credentials, fixed activation codes, server constants and customer-specific scenarios are not portable test fixtures. Replace them with customer configuration and run-owned inputs.
Treat simulator/hardening incompatibility as a prerequisite failure, not an SDK login defect. Retest with an artifact-supported destination.
Never recommend SuperApp Login V2 for native Android/iOS; test the selected native journey.

iOS FlowTests resetMasterController has no active reset implementation; resetApp/shutdown are commented and UI teardown is empty. Define an explicit owned-fixture reset rather than assuming setUp/tearDown isolates runs.

iOS checked-continuation error paths can call XCTFail without resuming. Resolve every success/error path exactly once and provide an overall timeout; failing an assertion alone does not unblock the await.
iOS nonoptional-result XCTAssertNotNil and transaction-finished expectation fulfillment do not verify SDK success. Assert concrete result type/status and transaction identity.
iOS wrong-activation-code helper checks contents only if an alert exists. Require a bounded wait with mandatory failure when the expected error UI is absent.
Do not copy broad keychain/sandbox deletion helpers or an unbounded SpringBoard uninstall loop. Scope reset to the dedicated app/test-owned records and bound its duration.
Never disable useTokenBasedLogin to work around ast_login_with_unactivated_client; this skips IAM setup and can cause CannotAcquireTokenData(50). Investigate the selected native backend flow instead.

Swift: switch on KssIdpStatus.success/eventFailed/requestFailed; never infer success from text containing accept. Preserve detailed callback status, errorCode and underlying event without logging tokens or credentials.

platform_notes.android: GSA uses app/src/testShift model tests; integratedUnitTest for SDK-event tests; integratedUiTest with Espresso/Kaspresso/UIAutomator and sharedintegrationtestsources; positiveflowtest for combined UI/backend flows. integratedUiTest targets :app, AndroidJUnitRunner and AndroidX Test Orchestrator with clearPackageData=true. Its connected-test hooks disable device animations persistently: record and restore original settings. Discover actual tasks using ./gradlew :integratedUiTest:tasks --all; do not assume GSA module names exist in a fresh customer app.
platform_notes.ios: GSA workspace GettingStarted_UI_Tests.xcworkspace has GettingStarted_FlowTests (direct real-SDK XCTest integration, not pure unit tests), GettingStarted_ShiftUITests (XCUITest) and GettingStarted_DigitaniumUITests (separate family; do not substitute). FlowTests uses TestPlanFlowTests and Shift UI uses TestPlanShiftUITests. Shared helpers provide bounded UI predicates and kept screenshot attachments. Properties tests check typed results/exact status and set/get round trips. Shift scenario sources cover activation, invalid code, login, wrong PIN, change PIN, reactivation, registration keystore variants, user deletion, transaction approve/decline, delivery while logged out, multiple transactions, background/resume and WebView mode. Source presence is not run coverage. Default Shift plan skips add-many-users and wrong-PIN-until-blocked. Serialize unless SDK singleton, app container and backend fixtures are isolated per worker.

android.code:
# Discover tasks before selecting a Shift test variant.
./gradlew :integratedUiTest:tasks --all
# In the GSA layout, after confirming this task and selecting a dedicated device:
ANDROID_SERIAL="$TEST_DEVICE_SERIAL" ./gradlew :integratedUiTest:connectedShiftDebugAndroidTest
# For a fresh app, replace the module/variant with its discovered instrumentation task.
# Collect runner XML/HTML results and SDK events/logs before clearing test data.

ios.code:
# From the GSA test workspace directory; first discover supported schemes/destinations.
xcodebuild -list -workspace GettingStarted_UI_Tests.xcworkspace
xcodebuild -showdestinations -workspace GettingStarted_UI_Tests.xcworkspace -scheme GettingStarted_ShiftUITests
# Set TEST_DESTINATION to the caller-selected, artifact-supported device;
# TEST_RESULT_BUNDLE must be a fresh output path.
xcodebuild test -workspace GettingStarted_UI_Tests.xcworkspace \
  -scheme GettingStarted_ShiftUITests -testPlan TestPlanShiftUITests \
  -destination "$TEST_DESTINATION" -parallel-testing-enabled NO \
  -resultBundlePath "$TEST_RESULT_BUNDLE"
# Direct SDK integration uses scheme GettingStarted_FlowTests / plan TestPlanFlowTests.
# In a fresh customer app, discover and substitute its own UI-test scheme/plan.
# Collect .xcresult, redacted SDK event evidence and encrypted SDK logs before reset.

checklist: Test manifest identifies SDK artifact, app revision, destination and selected native flow without secrets.
Unit, SDK integration and UI/backend test results are reported separately; skipped/ignored cases are visible.
Fresh Start and activation verify SDK state/result and owned backend device association.
Cold returning login preserves activated data across process restart and verifies the same user.
TMS checks both SDK and backend terminal state for the same transaction.
Negative cases have isolated fixtures and assert no unintended activation/login transition.
All asynchronous waits are bounded and listeners observe both success and failure events.
Failure evidence contains errorType, errorDescription, unsigned errorCode and SDK archive before reset.
Cleanup runs on failure, affects only owned fixtures and restores changed device settings.
